channel.title: Ekansh Sharma
channel.description: Machine learning researcher and engineer specializing in large-scale sequential modeling, optimization geometry, low-precision training numerics, and statistical inference.

item.title: June 2026 — News Update
item.description: Our preprint TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems is now available on arXiv.

item.title: May 2026 — News Update
item.description: My joint work with Mohammed Adnan, Rohan Jain, Tom Jacobs, Rahul G. Krishnan, Rebekka Burkholz, and Yani Ioannou on SparseOpt: Addressing Normalization-induced Gradient Skew in Sparse Training is accepted to ICML 2026.

item.title: November 2025 — News Update
item.description: Ph.D. in Computer Science conferred at the University of Toronto. Thesis: Exploiting linear connectivity modulo permutations in neural networks for parsimonious machine learning.

item.title: September 2025 — News Update
item.description: Started at Google as a Machine Learning Engineer working on large-scale recommender systems for YouTube Shorts.

item.title: May 2025 — News Update
item.description: My joint work with Mohammed Adnan, Rohan Jain, Rahul G. Krishnan, and Yani Ioannou on Sparse Training from Random Initialization: Aligning Lottery Ticket Masks using Weight Symmetry is accepted to ICML 2025.

item.title: January 2025 — News Update
item.description: Entered the job market following my Ph.D. research (archived milestone — see my updated CV).

item.title: December 2024 — News Update
item.description: My joint work with Mohammed Adnan, Rohan Jain, and Yani Ioannou on Winning Tickets from Random Initialization: Aligning Masks for Sparse Training is accepted to the UniREPS workshop at NeurIPS 2024.

item.title: October 2024 — News Update
item.description: New preprint on The Non-Local Model Merging Problem: Permutation Symmetries and Variance Collapse is out on arXiv, with code open-sourced in tact-merge.

item.title: May 2024 — News Update
item.description: My joint work with Devin Kwok, Tom Denton, Daniel M. Roy, David Rolnick, and Gintare K. Dziugaite on Simultaneous Linear Connectivity of Neural Networks Modulo Permutation is accepted to ECML PKDD 2024.

item.title: November 2023 — News Update
item.description: Our work on Simultaneous Linear Connectivity of Neural Networks Modulo Permutation was accepted for a non-archival spotlight at CPAL 2024.
